audit.whatIsWrong: Every one of the seven chart rows contradicted the whys[] sentence printed beside it. The page said Skill at Levels 1-2 while whys[0] and whys[1] both say Gwen wins them; it said Gwen at Levels 3, 4-5 and 6 while whys[2], whys[3] and whys[4] all call those skill windows; it said Gwen at first item while whys[5] says you all-in cleanly there; it said Yone at two items while whys[6] says it stays skill-dependent.
audit.why: The packet chart — Gwen, Gwen, Skill, Skill, Skill, Yone, Skill — agrees with the prose on all seven rows, and the 52.56% win rate over 1115 games supports a lane that starts against you and evens out.
audit.corrected: Gwen, Gwen, Skill, Skill, Skill, Yone, Skill, proposed as one atomic group across both layers.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns anywhere, and the first-item row was scored as a Gwen spike against the page's own text.
audit.why: Hallowed Mist is 22s at rank 1 falling only to 18s — the longest window in her kit and the one your all-in lives in. Skip 'n Slash is 13s to 11s and refunds part of its cooldown when she hits something. Snip Snip! is 6.5s down to 3.5s. Needlework is 120/100/80 and casts up to three times. Your Soul Unbound falls 22s to 10s; Fate Sealed is 120s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Your window is the 22-second Hallowed Mist gap; hers is any moment you stand in the mist with Snip Snip! up.

audit.whatIsWrong: Fate Sealed described as setting up team knockups; Hallowed Mist described only as 'she's safe inside'; the whole page's advice is 'build MR' against a champion whose Q core deals true damage.
audit.why: Hallowed Mist makes Gwen untargetable to anything outside it — that is a hard block on Fate Sealed, which needs a champion to target, not merely a damage reduction. Snip Snip!'s centre deals TRUE damage and applies her passive per snip, so magic resist does nothing about the part that kills you. A Thousand Cuts heals her off champion damage, which is what makes Grievous Wounds core. Skip 'n Slash applies on-hit effects and partially refunds itself on a hit, so it comes back faster in a trade than its 13s suggests. Fate Sealed blinks behind the last champion in a line and pulls — no airborne; your knockup is Mortal Steel at two stacks.
audit.corrected: You cannot target her through the mist at all, Fate Sealed included — bait or wait out the 22 seconds. MR blunts her passive and Skip 'n Slash, not the true-damage centre of Snip Snip!, so anti-heal and raw damage matter more than stacking resistances.

audit.whatIsWrong: Ability name written as 'Snip Snip' in spikes[0] and elsewhere.
audit.why: The real name carries the exclamation mark: Snip Snip!.

notes: All seven chart rows disagreed with the whys[] text sitting beside them, and the packet chart matched the prose exactly on all seven — flipped as one atomic group in both layers. The biggest mechanical gain here is that Hallowed Mist blocks TARGETING from outside, not just damage: Fate Sealed needs a champion to target, so it is a hard denial rather than a damage race. Left alone: the page-wide 'build MR' framing in tldr, winCon, report[0], report[1] and dosFull[1].t. It is only half right — MR does blunt her passive and Skip 'n Slash, but Snip Snip!'s centre is true damage — and rewriting those five short fields inside the length band would have cost more than the correction is worth. Mirror conflict noted: the audited Gwen page cites a 58.7% Gwen win rate while this packet gives Yone 52.56% over 1115 games; I aligned to this packet because it agrees with this page's own prose row for row.
